source.section: PIT-ADJ instructions PDF page 5, line 16; Form PIT-1 lines 9 to 18 and 22; instructions PDF page 25, line 12; Tax Rate Table PDF pages 1 to 6, rows; PDF page 7 (T-7), over 100,000

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 50,000.00 + long-term gains 1,000.00 = 51,000.00. Federal taxable income = 51,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 35,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Form PIT-1 takes only the federal line 12 amount, and no line for what the federal return subtracts after line 12). Form PIT-1, married filing separately. Line 9 federal AGI 51,000.00. Line 10 0.00 (standard deduction taken). Line 11 additions 0.00. Line 12 federal standard deduction 15,750.00. Line 13 dependents 0.00. Line 14 0.00: federal AGI 51,000.00 is over the worksheet's printed ceiling 27,500.00 for this status, so the worksheet is not completed. Line 15, PIT-ADJ: line 16 net capital gains: smaller of 1,000.00 and the cap 1,250.00 = 1,000.00; PIT-ADJ line 28 total 1,000.00. Line 17 = 51,000.00 + 0.00 - 15,750.00 - 0.00 - 1,000.00 = 34,250.00. By the projection: state_agi = federal taxable income 35,250.00 - 1,000.00 = 34,250.00; less base deductions 0.00 gives 34,250.00. Line 18 tax, schedule as numbers: 1.5% x 4,000.00 = 60 + 3.2% x 8,500.00 = 272 + 4.3% x 12,500.00 = 537.5 + 4.7% x 9,250.00 = 434.75; total 1,304.25, to the cent 1,304.25. The table row over 34,200 to 34,300 gives 1,304; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 19 to 21 0.00. Line 22 net New Mexico income tax 1,304.25.
